definition: Unproductive consumption that serves no utilitarian end — luxury, war, spectacle, sacrifice, eroticism, art; Bataille argues that economists undervalue expenditure because the primus motor of economic life is not production and accumulation but the movement and dissipation of excess energy, inverting the logic of restricted economy

definition: The condition of existing without subordination to utility, purpose, or the future — sovereignty is the refusal of servile instrumentality, an experience in which thought and reason are brought to the point where they dissolve into nothing; not political domination but the moment of useless, purposeless existence that escapes the logic of means and ends

definition: An economic theory that takes as its starting point not scarcity and rational allocation but the excess of energy produced by the sun — societies inevitably generate more resources than survival requires, and this surplus must be spent unproductively (in art, eroticism, spectacle, war) or it will erupt catastrophically; general economy encompasses restricted economy as a special case
connective_patterns: general economy begins from surplus rather than scarcity
general economy encompasses restricted economy

definition: The conventional economic perspective focused on production, accumulation, conservation, and rational allocation of scarce resources — what Bataille considers a partial and derivative view that represses the fundamental reality of excess; restricted economy treats expenditure as a means to accumulation rather than recognizing expenditure as primary
connective_patterns: restricted economy as partial view of general economy

definition: The surplus energy produced by living systems beyond what is needed for survival — the fundamental condition of life according to Bataille's cosmological perspective; excess is not a deficiency to be corrected but the primary datum of existence, and the central problem of any society is how to expend its surplus rather than how to produce enough
connective_patterns: excess as the fundamental condition of life
the problem of how to expend excess energy
excess energy that must be spent luxuriously or catastrophically

definition: Following Durkheim's sacred/profane distinction, the domain of the extraordinary, dangerous, and contagious that is set apart from the mundane order of work and reason; the sacred is experienced through transgression of taboos, sacrifice, and festival — moments in which the discontinuity of individual existence is dissolved into a terrifying continuity that is both destructive and regenerative

the sacred as the domain of excess and violence

definition: The violation of taboos that paradoxically completes and reaffirms them — transgression is not mere rebellion but a dynamic interplay with prohibition; taboos demand transgression to fulfill their function, and the temporary lifting of prohibitions (in festival, sacrifice, eroticism) opens a space of sacred excess that sustains the social order it appears to threaten

definition: A privileged example of how human beings relate to excess and expenditure — eroticism confronts the individual with the dissolution of discontinuous existence into continuity, evoking both death and ecstasy; not merely sexuality but the domain where taboo and transgression, individual boundaries and their dissolution, are experienced most intensely

definition: A non-discursive limit-experience in which the subject is brought to the point of dissolution — neither mystical union with God nor philosophical self-reflection but the suppression of discursive thought that opens onto the void; inner experience refuses all external authority and all projects, existing as sovereign purposelessness that confronts the impossibility of knowledge at its own limit

definition: That which is inassimilable to the homogeneous order of production, rationality, and social utility — the sacred, the abject, the excessive, the violent; heterogeneous elements are expelled from or repressed by the social body precisely because they resist integration into the functional, productive, rational order of modern society

definition: The ceremonial practice of competitive gift-giving and destruction of wealth among Northwest Coast peoples — Bataille uses it as the paradigmatic example of expenditure in pre-capitalist societies, where social rank is determined not by accumulation but by the capacity to give away or destroy surplus, demonstrating sovereignty through the renunciation of utility

definition: The portion of surplus energy that a society must expend unproductively — either knowingly through luxury, art, spectacle, and non-procreative sexuality, or unknowingly through catastrophic eruptions of war and destruction; the accursed share is cursed because it cannot be saved or invested, only spent or suffered
